title: How 'Charleston's Ghost Girl' is shedding light on the city's dark and haunted history
excerpt: Through her paranormal podcast and investigation videos, Kelsey Nyx is educating audiences about Charleston's dark history and haunted locations. She shared her investigation process and scariest experiences.
content:
Kelsey Nyx doesn't think her childhood home in Moncks Corner was haunted, but she does think something supernatural was attached to her family. 

Lights flickered. Toys turned on and off on their own. Strange noises echoed in hallways. 

With such a spooky upbringing, Nyx easily could have shied away from otherworldly entities. Instead, she developed a fascination with the unexplained. These days, she's made a career out of talking to ghosts. 

Nyx, also known as "Charleston's Ghost Girl", has been a full-time paranormal investigator and podcaster for about a year. In that time, she's attempted to communicate with spirits in old farmhouses, cemeteries, historic homes and Charleston landmarks such as the Old City Jail and John Rutledge House Inn.

"It's been like a little dream come true," Nyx said. 

A few months ago, Nyx announced a partnership with Ghost City Tours, a national tour company that specializes in haunted history. Charissa Lauren, public relations manager for the company, said Charleston is one of its biggest markets, so having a designated paranormal partner in the city made sense. 

Ghost City Tours hopes to expand Nyx's network and platform as a content creator and host her at various investigations and events. Lauren said Nyx is a joy to work with and a talented investigator and creator.

"I honestly can't think of a better storyteller than Kelsey in Charleston right now," she said. 

How to talk to ghosts

Nyx does very little research on a haunted location before beginning her investigation. That helps prevent prior knowledge and preconceived notions from influencing the evidence she collects.

Then, once her investigation has concluded, she conducts research on the location's history and looks for connections with the information she gathered during her visit.

"Nine times out of 10 you’re making those connections, and that’s the mind-blowing part of it," Nyx said. 

Nyx views a paranormal investigation as a serious and sometimes delicate process. It's not something to jump into without preparation, she said. 

Before exploring a haunted location, Nyx first ensures she is calm and grounded. Then she announces her intentions to the spirits. She makes it clear that she isn't there to harm or disturb them but is open to communicating with them if they choose to engage. 

Next, she sets up her equipment. 

There is a host of tools paranormal investigators use to detect and communicate with the other side, but Nyx finds herself returning to a core group: two flashlights, an electromagnetic field (EMF) reader and a spirit box.

The flashlight method involves adjusting a twist-top flashlight to balance precariously between the on and off settings, so spirits can easily manipulate the flickers of light.

Nyx typically uses two flashlights. If one is manipulated, it indicates a "yes" response. If the other flickers, that means "no."

EMF readers light up when they detect a fluctuation in electromagnetic fields, which paranormal investigators believe can be caused by spirits. 

Spirit boxes, also known as ghost boxes, are modified radios that rapidly sweep through frequencies to produce white noise and audio fragments. Some believe spirits can use the electromagnetic energy to control the words which come through. 

“It’s definitely not a cheap hobby, but it is worth it to get the reaction and getting the questions answered that you want," Nyx said. 

Rather than asking hard-hitting questions right away, Nyx allows the spirits to guide the conversation. Often, they want to share details of their life with her. Sometimes, the conversation takes a darker turn. 

Enigmatic encounters

Nyx said she rarely gets spooked, but one investigation in particular left her rattled. She and a friend made contact with a spirit in a Charleston cemetery (Nyx chose not to disclose its name out of respect for those buried there) and began receiving responses that indicated an evil and potentially demonic presence.

She heard rustling and footsteps beside her, then the sound of something charging in her direction. 

That left her shaken, although it wasn't enough to keep her away from the cemetery. 

“I just recently went alone and I was like, ‘Yeah, no. This will probably be the last time I come out here at night alone,'" she said. 

Most interactions aren't threatening, though. For instance, Nyx believes she may have contacted the late John Rutledge, the first official governor of South Carolina and a signer of the U.S. Constitution, while investigating his former home at 116 Broad St. 

Nyx asked if Rutledge was in the room, and a flashlight lit up to indicate “yes.” Then she heard the name John Rutledge come through on the spirit box several times, she said. 

“It was very active … Immediately when I started setting up, devices were going off before I could even hit record,” Nyx said.

Using the flashlight method, she was also able to confirm that parts of the Constitution were drafted in the second-floor ballroom known as the Signer's Ballroom, she said.

You can find her investigation of the John Rutledge House Inn, as well as many other investigation videos, on her YouTube channel (@Kelsey_nyx). 

Afterlife lessons

Studying the paranormal has raised more questions than answers for Nyx. She said it's altered her perspective on life, religion and death and has challenged her beliefs. 

Ironically, one of the most profound lessons she's learned has to do with the living people in her life. 

Pursuing a profession that's outside of the norm has come with challenges, she said. She's come to understand that not everyone agrees with her path or takes it as seriously as she does. At times, she’s struggled to find people who support her.

But that's never dissuaded her.

“I have a passion for it. I have something calling me to this,” she said. “I know this is my path, and I’m just going to do it.”

One of the things that drives Nyx's work is her dedication to discussing Charleston's dark history. 

From the numerous burial grounds beneath Charleston to the city's role in the transatlantic slave trade, Nyx said it's important to remember the past. 

Lauren agreed. 

"I think it's so important to learn about not just the haunted history, but history in general," she said.

For Charleston's Ghost Girl, that means getting up close and personal with those who lived it.
